product_title: Haier HVTM12DABB 12-Bottle Dual Zone Mirrored Glass Door Wine Cellar
review_headline: we absolutely loved it. (And our thanks go out to the ...
review_body:
We ordered this wine cellar in March 2013. Until about one month ago, we absolutely loved it. (And our thanks go out to the many reviews we read before we purchased it -- those reviews were not only helpful, but definitive in helping us make our choice.) I'll start my review with the positives, because our problems might be unique to our model; others might find the positives worth looking at.

Arrival: When it first arrived, we were impressed with the build - compact, hefty, and even cute.

Storage: We loved the fact that we could store open bottles of wine in the fridge, even though our re-usable corks are quite long. The fridge accommodated those long corks with no problem. (Of course, we had to make sure that the corks were placed snugly in the bottles; otherwise, we risked wine spilling out of the bottles as they lay on their sides.)

Temps: The fridge kept temperatures fairly well, even though we live in the desert, where outside temps can go as high as 45° C. The temps did sometimes creep up a bit when it was hot *and* humid outside, but that seemed reasonable for an inexpensive product.

Noise: Most frequently the fridge was quiet. Sometimes on Sunday mornings, we could hear some whirring from rooms other than where we keep the fridge, but that's when neighborhood noise and other ambient noise was at its lowest point. And the whirring wasn't unbearable - just a bit noticeable.

Bottom line for fridge, until September 2014: For 18 months, we loved our little wine fridge.

Current evaluation: Unusable. About one month ago, the fridge started making horrible noises that we could hear throughout the house. Indeed, the noises woke us up sometimes at night. In response, we unplugged the fridge to let it "rest" (and to give us some peace for a bit); we left it unplugged for a couple of days. After plugging it back in, we got a few more days of quiet usage. But then the fridge startedshrieking and grinding again. We repeated the unplug-replug cycle over the course of the last month (which isn't very good for the stored wines), and we've finally given up. We're really sad, because we loved our little wine fridge.

review_headline: DON'T BUY!!! unless your into MODIFICATION!!!! POOR air circulation when filled up!!
review_body: Any review that says this works GOOD out of the box hasn't done any testing! At least in a similar environment as I am in. I live in the desert with evaporative cooling. That means good luck keeping your cigar under 70 F in the summer. I've measured Temp and Humidity on all shelves simultaneously even at the bottom with NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) traceable calibrated devices. Although when empty temp and humidity are more constant. The purpose of the device is to fill it up with cigars and create a micro climate suitable for storage of cigars. If the humidor is full there is little to no circulation of air. Temp differences of up to 10 degrees F and humidity up to 20% from top to bottom when humidor is full.  Humidor needs air circulation even if it is satisfied temperature wise. There are no allowances for this. When the thermo electric devices is activated (transferring heat) it acts as a dehumidifier. This product was made with out any thought. It's just a thermo electric wine cooler with cedar shelves. Guess what? Wine is in a sealed bottle (It's own micro climate) cigars are not!!! You are supposed to be creating a micro climate for the cigars. I am currently modifying mine with extra fans an a controller (AC Infinity AI-ATC, Fan Thermostat and Speed Controller with two sets of AI-MPF80A2 Quiet Dual 80mm). I hope this will work but I still have to overcome the lack of space (when full) around the shelves for air movement. I will update this post to let people know how the modification turns out. product_title: Samsung Neat White 5.0 Cu Ft Top Load Washer and 7.4 Cu Ft Steam Electric Dryer WA50F9A6DSW DV50F9A6EVW
review_headline: SAMSUNG customer service works for Samsung, not you.  Know what to look for in a bad unit - read this review.
review_body:
ALERT ALERT ALERT - BEFORE YOU BUY A SAMSUNG READ THIS - ALERT ALERT ALERT
Hi folks - I hate to be an alarmist, but I have information you NEED TO KNOW about Samsung and other washing machines of this general manufacture. I bought the 50 version of this washer (WA50) and after 2 years it failed. It wasn't anything we did, it was a KNOWN issue with the manufacture of the machine. You see, when it's ready to drain there's a pump that pushes the water out the exhaust tube into your drain pipe.
THAT PUMP can easily crack, break, and fail - causing the machine to dump all it's water onto the ground.
Until that happened this was a perfect washing machine for our family, worked flawlessly, saved water and energy, we were happy.
How can you know if you got a model with the crappy drain pump? In general the crappy pump is attached to the tub itself, right on the drum. You simply tilt your machine up and look. Follow the water exhaust/discharge hose from the outside of your machine to a cylindrical device that's (hopefully) attached to a hose that goes to the drum. If the pump is on the drum, you got a bad one!
The Samsung repair guy came out to repair mine and told me all about this issue. I asked what makes the decision whether you repair one out of warranty (I was at 2 years the machine has a 1 year warranty - because the pump isn't part of the DRIVE TRAIN 10 year warranty.) His response: whether the customer complains enough.
Yes, my machine got fixed - but the customer service gave me a serious run around (over 4 hours on the phone). One of the managers even had the audacity to call me, and left me the wrong return phone number THREE TIMES!!! (*or does Samsung market time shares?)
Their stellar lack of customer service and desire not to stand by their defective merchandise has earned Samsung this negative review and my warning. Be sure your pump is mounted to the machine frame at the base of the unit NOT THE DRUM. It makessense if you think about it. The drum sees a lot of vibration, a plastic pump mounted to that vibrating behemoth is bound to fail.

product_title: midea WHD-113F Double Reversible Door Refrigerator and Freezer, 3.1 Cubic Feet, Black
review_headline: Let me tell you, this little unit is THE ONE.
review_body:
You can find this model at a big-box store for less, and they offer free shipping as well. But I came to Amazon first to read reviews and browse before looking up the model number online for the best price once I found which one I liked.

I had first narrowed my search of MINI fridges down to ones with a separate freezer. I find the built-in freezer section on other units always freezes up and intrudes on the fridge space, and isn't all that big to begin with. I also wanted something usable for more than just left-over-lunch and a gatorade - something around 3 cubic feet.

I looked at a bunch of units and I'm pretty sure they are almost all the same design made in China, with minor differences. I'm almost certain that the same factory makes all of these units and sells them to other companies that slap their name on the front. I saw one with a cute through-door water-dispenser, so if a major use would be using the fridge for ice-cold water that unit would be nice. The other difference I noted was in the fridge door - some have room for a 5-can stack and a full width tray at the top of the door, and some have room for a 6-can stack and a half-width tray at the top of the door. I thought 6 cans would be better than 5, since that tray is so small not fits there anyway.

Midea offers three versions of this same unit - all white, all black, and black with the door panels covered in stainless steel. I opted for all black, since its cheaper and blends in better. This unit isn't quite small enough to fit under my counter, but sits next to my desk and I can use the top of him as additional horizontal storage for a coffee maker, toaster oven, or what-have-you.

Let me summarize the rest of this review

PROS :
Super low energy usage. Some of the other mini-fridges in this class use ~$36/yr, this one uses only $29/yr.

Runs (down to) very cold. On Max the fridge is @ 38° and the freezer is at 25° when the ambient temp is 88°.

Separate freezer space. The freezer stays ice-cold and no frost in the fridge area. The freezer space is about 15 inches deep, 7 inches high, and 18 inches wide. The door takes away about 3 inches of depth for the shelf on the door.

Spacious. You can actually fit quite a bit in the fridge section. If you take out the middle glass shelf, you can fit larger objects like pots of chili and opened wine bottles.

Quiet. This is about as silent as a low-energy fridge can be. It is similar to a small aquarium air-pump, or a desktop computer. Fifteen feet away from it and I can only _just_ hear it. This mini-fridge doesn't have an evaporator with a fan blowing over it to remove heat, thereby reducing power consumption and noise, it simply radiates the heat out of the side panels which act as a giant heat-sink.

Door organizer. Holds a 6-pack of cans plus a half gallon of milk and a 2L bottle all at once with a tiny shelf space to spare.

Features. The vegetable crisper will keep loose wilty food in a higher humidity environment so they last longer. Built-in light is a nice touch. Glass shelves instead of wire racks. Comes with a small plastic ice scraper when you need to manually defrost the freezer, and a small ice-cube rack (6x2 mini cubes). Nice long power cord - about 36 inches. Plastic drip tray over the compressor for catching condensation from the auto-defrost of the fridge.

Packaging. This was shipped by FedEx to my home, and although the box is big and about 60lbs, it surprisingly wasn't crushed or looked damaged. The packing is a hard-plastic bottom tray lined in styrofoam that the fridge sits on. Over that was a one-piece 5-sided double-wall of cardboard that had a styrofoam liner inside protecting the fridge. The bottom was strapped to the top with bands. All the pieces of the fridge (door, shelves, etc) were taped up and packed with cardboard spacers around them. The item arrived inperfect condition (no marks), and worked on plugging it in.

CONS

The crisper doesn't have any humidity control, so don't put food that ripens in it as trapped ethylene gas will accelerate the ripening. If you like cold fruit like bananas and pears, buy some "blue apples" to absorb ethylene gas.

Manual thermostat control feels dated, although it does the job, and no digital temperature display or humidity display. I bought a separate digital unit by Andoer.

Doors held shut by magnets, not by latches. Magnets are not rare-earth, and are not the strongest. If your fridge is usually bursting with food, the light-weight doors might have trouble staying shut. You might need something like XtraGuard latches, Safety 1st appliance lock or fridge latch.

The soda-can holder is a nice feature, but if you don't drink canned drinks its a total waste of space. Also, this model chooses to hold 6 cans instead of 5, which means the shelf at the top of the door is only half-width, making it mostly useless. I keep a block of cream cheese on it for some bagels, and that's about all that will fit there. You'll have to choose what you will do with that space - besides a stick of butter, a block of cream cheese, or maybe a bag of candy or pair of jello dessert cups not much fits that tiny tray space.

----

The unit itself is not designed to be a built-in. You can feel the heat given off on the sides, and the compressor at the bottom/back needs ventilation. Understand that a compressor-driven refrigerator doesn't just "make" cold, it simply moves heat out of the box making the inside cold and therefore venting heat to the outside. Make sure there is room on the sides of the fridge to vent that heat, or else the heat will stay in the box and try to warm up the fridge and then the compressor will be fighting against itself. If you keep the sides vented it should prolong the life of the unit. Also, notrunning the fridge on high will extend the life of the compressor. The compressor has a 5-year MTBF rating, and I would think that would be normal to expect for the life of this unit. These are sealed system units with no way to service them, and unfortunately, a new compressor is about the cost of the unit. Adding in labor and such makes it cheaper to dispose of these units than to fix them.

product_title: KRUPS and HEINEKEN B100 BeerTender with Heineken Draught Keg Technology,Black
review_body:
I recently replaced my Edgestar mini-keg with the Krups and am liking the Krups much better. Note Newcastle is one of my favorite beers - if you don't like Newcastle or Heineken don't buy either of them.

Edgestar advantages: can use any minikeg with the conversion kit, in theory. I have the conversion kit, and found it leaked CO2 as the parts are cheaply made. A single CO2 cartridge lasted only a day or two then needed to be replaced. Even with the kit the beer selection isn't great. My Edgestar did last over 3.5 years, so not bad.
Edgestar disadvantages: you have to clean the lines, thoroughly with vinegar, every time you change the keg, or it will plug (and your beer will taste lousy). The cleaning bottle is a piece of junk and cracks after a few uses, then you have to improvise. It's really a pain. The plastic taps are prone to breakage; replacements are hard to find and expensive - I had to call/email Edgestar customer support repeatedly after the news ones I ordered were all defective (they did send me replacements). Fairly loud, like a mini-fridge. Tap doesn't lock open and pours slowly resulting in foamy beers. Changing the tap sometimes helps.

Krups advantages: pours faster, tap locks open, resulting in less foam. Costs $50 less (everywhere but Amazon). Quiet - makes no noise. As you replace the tap/line with each keg you don't have to clean the lines. Many people feel this is a disadvantage, but unless you're really strapped for cash this is a huge advantage. For one, less cleaning. Second, the line is always new and clean. I will gladly pay a dollar and change to NOT have to clean the lines after each keg. Spill tray is larger and higher quality. Design is more modern.
Krups disadvantages: many reviews complain it only lasts a year+, so I bought mine at Best Buy and shelled out the $15 for the two year protection plan. You do have to replace the line with each keg (or clean it), but the new tubes are so cheap I probably spent more on replacement parts for my Egdestar.

review_headline: Going to make this simple and sweet. My refrigerator's ice maker broke and I didn't ...
review_body: Going to make this simple and sweet. My refrigerator's ice maker broke and I didn't want to spend $100's to get someone to fix it at the time. Also, the ice in fridge comes from my sink and the water is terrible, so the ice isn't great. Even with the fridge filter, the ice still tasted funny. So I decided to buy this NewAir 28LB Icemaker machine. I've had it for 8 months now and I've only had one problem with it once. One time I turned it on and I noticed the fan wasn't running. The unit was on and water had sucked up into the machine, but I wasn't sure if it would make any ice if the fan wasn't running. I turned it off and put it back on and the same thing happened. It still produced ice though. After about 30 mins, I turned it off and pulled the plug out on it. Let is sit for 15 mins. Then plugged it in and turned it back on. After about 5 mins the fan came back on and it's been working fine since. It constantly makes ice and only takes about an 45-60 mins to fill the tray. So in about 3-4 hrs my fridge is filled with ice and I don't have to worry about it for 4-5 days. I did get an extended warranty on it. So after a year is over, my extended warranty kicks in and if it breaks I can get it replaced or repaired for free. I'm hoping it never breaks though. Many reviewers have said theirs started to break 12-18 month after steady use. So we'll see. I'll update my review in about 6-8 months from now.

review_body: We wanted a small refrigerator for beer and wine, and have had very good luck with past Danby products. The Amazon product page for this model is a bit confusing as the picture with the door open shows slots for the shelves, and then below it talks about a different model, the DAR044A4WDD showing shelves that snap into rear tracks! Giggling the electrical cord it would turn on briefly. Upon further investigation by removing the back cover where the hose/plug routes through their was scorch marks on the 3-wire coupling plug going from the power cord to the internal wiring (about 14 inches from the top of the machine). Disconnecting the coupling the internal male end crimp was not seated all the way, pushing the connectors in the coupling all the way and taping the wires in place solved all power issues with unit shutting off/no power. Will say this happens if you pull the cord too far out and the turns the cord takes inside the back of the machine causes the inside wire to pull out of the coupling connector.

product_title: The pureWash Professional-Grade Ionic Laundry Purifier (High-Efficiency Washers)
review_headline: Decent product, based on my experience
review_body:
I've been using the PureWash in my front-loader for three or four months now, with mostly good results.

The main positives in my experience:

1) It's easy to install, so long as you can get at the cold water line that feeds your washer, and so long as you can get by without installing a prefilter on the water line. (More about that, below.)

2) It takes only about 60 watts to operate, and it operates only while the machine fills, so the energy costs are minimal.

3) The washer runs on just cold water, avoiding the cost of heating water for laundry. This is a major money saver, depending on the volume of water involved.

4) No more detergent and fabric softener resides in the clothing or in the machine. My machine had begun to build up a brownish film in certain areas, but after using the PureWash for a while, that gradually disappeared. In fact, after the first couple of uses, there was some of this crud collecting in the tub, and I needed to wipe it out -- it probably came from the inner parts of the washer. It did take several washings of old towels in the PureWash water before they stopped being crispy from old detergent residues left in them from earlier days. (I haven't used fabric softener for a long time, since the residues mess with my skin, and I don't use dryer sheets for the same reason, so old towels were getting crispy in the drier.)

5) After multiple washings in PureWash water, some of the brownish stains from body oils on older whites disappeared. I had never been able to get those out before with detergent and clorine-free bleach. Underarm odors are also pretty well removed -- much better than with unscented detergent.

6) It's great not to have more detergent gunk sent off to my septic system to muck up the works there. Septic systems are very expensive to fix once they get plugged up with hardened chemical residues. We're talking about real money here.

7) After they've been washed several times with PureWash, stuff comes out of the dryer soft, without using any dryer sheets. (If you look into the chemical composition of dryer sheets, you'll not want to keep using them on anything you put next to your skin.)

8) If for some reason you want to wash something without using the PureWash system, you can just unplug it from the electrical supply to turn it off.

However, there are some negatives as well:

1) The PureWash generates ozone in the wash and rinse water. Ozone is great as an odor-remover and cleaner, just as PureWash advertises, but it is not going to stay just inside the washer, since washers are not air tight. Ozone is toxic to breathe, in high concentrations. My laundry room is about 100 square feet, with poor air circulation, and I could definitely smell the ozone in the air, and it was not the nice, fresh smell of the outdoors after a rainstorm, because it was much stronger. So, I set up a professional ozone meter and found that the ozone levels never exceeded the "short term" limits set by the feds for worker exposure, but did exceed the limits for 8-hour exposure by 50% toward the end of washing the first load. I found the levels irritating. Running the dryer quickly solves the problem, by sucking air out of the room, so it is possible to do one load after another by timing things right.

2) Whites do not get as white as washing with regular chlorine bleach (if you can stand to use that dangerous clothing-eating stuff). Perhaps that is due to the chemical composition of my water.

3) Buyers need to be aware that the hydroxyl and ozone produced by the PureWash will react negatively with certain chemicals in the water supply coming into the washer. PureWash recommends installing a prefilter, but I did not install one, since my wash water is free of sediment, free of chlorine, and free of rust and dissolved metals. (I have a well, and my water is all treated asit comes into the house.) I think the successful use of the PureWash depends on getting interfering chemicals out of the water. Since my water is highly softened, I think I'm getting some interaction between the softening ions and the PureWash water, since there is a tendency to get a little goo building up in the washer. This problem seems to be solved by rinsing the clothes an extra time with the PureWash unplugged, before they go off to the dryer.

4) Initial PureWash washings of items that have been washed repeatedly in detergents in the past may not be entirely good, since there are likely to be some undesireable byproducts produced when the PureWash water reacts with detergent residues. I'm not talking about damage to the washed items, but rather things like odd smells, or a little slippery-feeling residue that might irritate sensitive skin a little. This is a fairly minor issue for me, that gradually went away as the items were washed again.

I know some people say they put a little detergent into their wash water even when using the PureWash. That seems to me to be a bad idea. If there is some reason you want to use detergent, then use it in a separate washing with the PureWash unplugged.

The bottom line: using PureWash takes some adjusting of old habits, might take some effort, but the end result is well worth it, to me. Of course, if the PureWash machine were to break down in the first year, I'd change my mind, but so far, so good.

product_title: Danby 0.7 cu.ft. Countertop Microwave
review_headline: Do Not Like but Using It
review_body:
This is a terrible machine. The numbers on the keyboard are difficult to see. (I solved this problem by writing the numbers in dark ink on white pieces of paper and pasting the numbered papers to each appropriate number on the keyboard; a nuisance but it works well.) Next it is very difficult to program the machine! The numbers and choices are not touch sensitive—this makes it very difficult to enter your commands. Every time you want to make an entry it is a contest between your finger and the machine. If you expect a light finger touch to the keypad this machine is going to knock you out. Which brings me to the lever that opens the door? It is not touch sensitive either. Difficult to push it in, takes a good solid hard push; not a gentle push that a genteel person would like to use. (This microwave machine has replaced one exactly opposite to all the above remarks.)

Then there is the noise. I am referring to the binging that happens each time the time clock reaches zero. It cannot be turned off; I found if the machine is stopped manually one second before zero there is no binging. Then give a hard push to the ‘stop’ button and there is no need to listen to that raucous noise.

With a lot of practice I have learned to program the keypad so it is not as difficult to use as it was initially, but it will always be unpleasant to touch/push those numbers/choices. However, the machine only cost about a hundred dollars (not much for an important kitchen appliance) and does well the two basic jobs given it by me -- defrost food that comes directly from the freezer, heat food and water up. It also fits precisely in the small space that I have available for a microwave.

On high it is definitely audible but on par with what some hoods sound like on low. This is far quieter than the $1000 Ikea units or the high end hoods costing a couple grand.

Install was relatively straight forward and the unit is actually very well engineered inside.

I have two gripes with the unit; however. I installed it in a kitchen with a 8ft ceiling. I had to cut a large chuck of the internal frame to get 29in of clearance above my range. I ran out of factory holes then to attach it to the frame piece which attaches to the ceiling; I had to drill my own. The chimney covers worked just fine, on the other hand.

Finally, the operation is a little odd as you have to press the clock button to power on the hood to then use the + and - symbols to turn the fan up and down. If you hold the clock for just a little too long it will go into time set mode. It's not the end of the world but that part is not it's strength.

All in all, this is a very good hood for the price and if you shop around you can get it for quite a bargain.

product_title: Whirlpool WMC20005YB 0.5 Cu. Ft. Black Countertop Microwave
review_headline: Best microwave I've ever owned or used.
review_body:
This is by far the best microwave I've ever owned, of any size or price, for two reasons: (1) form factor and (2) simplicity of controls. I use a microwave to heat leftovers, cook frozen meals, make popcorn, melt butter or cheese, thaw frozen meat, reheat cold coffee, freshen stale bread of make it into croutons, cook sausages and hot dogs etc. I use this microwave several times per day. I think my microwave usage is pretty typical. The only thing I don't do in the microwave is prepare entrees from scratch (like cooking a roast or casserole). I've cooked all sizes of frozen entrees with no issues. Note, my review refers to an earlier model of this machine, which seems identical to this one that has replaced it.

(1) Form factor. Because the guts of the machine are under the cooking chamber, this has the smallest possible footprint. And because of the rounded back, I have it tucked into a corner of the countertop. This means I lose only 1' of countertop, and furthermore it's an awkward part of the countertop I wouldn't use for prep work etc because my elbow would bang into the fridge. Every other microwave I've ever owned took up 2' of prime, useable countertop. This makes such a huge difference in the usability and appearance of the kitchen that I'd give it five stars for this reason alone.

The interior size of this machine is bigger than you'd think because it's round and all the space is useable. The round turntable entirely fills the rounded shape of the interior. An advantage of this is that nothing falls off into the corners as it cooks. I've occasionally thawed something bigger then the turntable (the sides and front of the microwave are square so this is possible) and it wasn't a problem.

(2) Controls. I love love love the simplicity of the controls. It does exactly everything I need it to do in a way that is completely intuitive and simple. I should mention I own an Emerson microwave in my office that I have never yet beenable to figure out how to operate (and I'm of at least normal intelligence). The hated Emerson has lots of buttons and I'm sure it does a lot of things I don't need, but none of that matters because I'm not willing to learn a complex and counterintuitive interface to cook a frozen lunch entree. This Whirlpool, however, is amazing. It has Power, Defrost, Reheat and Popcorn buttons, as well as a Plus (+) and Minus (-) and a Start and a Stop. I accomplish everything with the Plus, Minus. Start and Stop, and occasionally Power.

To operate, you can just press the Plus until you reach the time you want, then press Start. Bam. You can't get any easier than that. The time increments get larger as you increase time, and this is absolutely not a problem. It uses 5 second increments up to 2 minutes, then 15 second increments to 3 minutes, then 30 second increments up to six minutes, then one minute increments from there. This is fine; I've never had an issue where using 6 or 7 minutes instead of 6.5 minutes caused a meal to fail (my pot pies call for 6.5 minutes at 50% power, and they're fine at either 6 or 7. When I make popcorn, I always listen to the popping and stop it when it slows. That's because popping times depend much more on the freshness and moisture content of the kernels than the power of the microwave; this is true of every microwave. Similarly, when I'm thawing something I pay attention to the progress of it because again, the fat content of the food and how hard it's frozen makes all the difference in timing. I suspect there are fancy convention microwaves with thermal probes that allow completely mindless use, but that kind of ultra high-end microwave isn't what I want or need.

I've been using an earlier model of this microwave for three years with absolutely no problem. I can't speak to specific reliability of the model here, but mine is the same in layout of controls, form factor, etc, so I would not hesitate to buy this one. In factI'm very tempted to buy one of these for the office and get rid of that annoying Emerson once and for all.

There was and still is a very loud squealing noise when opening the freezing drawer. It’s from the upper tray in the freezer. Called Samsung and they said it’s normal and can’t be repaired.

There's 2 ice cube making machines. 1 on the door and 1 inside the bottom freezer. The one on the bottom freezer is really loud when the ice cubes dump into the plastic tray.
The nice thing is this refrigerator is huge with lots of space and nice LED lighting. They shouldn't have wasted space on the water filter when it could be install outside of the refrigerator behind in the drywall pocket cutout or at the reverse osmosis filtration system. I'm not into drinking tap water or just using a 1 stage filter from Samsung.

In August 2014, I noticed the freezer door was really crooked, about ¼” gap at the top of the pull out freezer drawer while the bottom part had no gap when the door is fully closed.
And the now the right-side refrigerator door seal was leaking air.

On September 17, 2014 I called Samsung customer service. They said it’s out of warranty and will have to transfer me to Executive customer service department.
There they approved a one time warranty extension. Service transaction number: 4126641969

This time a 3rd party appliance company called
Service Quick, Inc
18655 Bishop Ave Carson, CA 90746
(310) 747-1360

On October 3, 2014 a repairman Raymond (senior tech) from Service Quick came out and found an error code regarding the defroster sensor. Oh that’s why some of the food in the refrigerator had ice on it!

He replaced the damaged refrigerator right seal.

About the bottom freezer door being crooked and leaking air. Raymond said it can’t be repaired and it’s not a problem. Unbelievable really!

Called Samsung Executive customer service department about the leaking bottom freezer door. First lady said it’s normal and not a big issue and will not do anything about it. She was mean and rude.

A minute later, I talked to a different guy from the Executive customer service department. He was really nice and concerned. He said Service Quick didn’t put in their report that the bottom door leakage was “non-repairable”.

So I called Service Quick and they said they will not put “non-repairable” in their report. Cold air is leaking, there’s a gap of about ¼”!
Their reason? They said it’s not an issue and to call Samsung and request another repair company.

It looks like Samsung and the 3rd party repair companies have some agreement to cut Samsung expenses?

The refrigerator is new with so many problems. It wasn’t cheap! $2500! I can see if it was a cheap refrigerator but it wasn’t.
You only have 1 year to find any problems. After that there’s a possible one time extension.

I thought Samsung being the largest tech company in Korea and heard good things about Samsung TV and cell phones that the refrigerators would be quality also. I thought wrong. Best to stick with quality American made (getting difficult to find but they’re out there), Japanese or German.

product_title: GE JVM3150RFSS 1.5 Cu. Ft. Stainless Steel Over-the-Range Microwave
review_body:
I am a little shocked by some of the, shall we say, less than flattering reviews here. I've had this microwave for several months now and aside from a couple of things I'm pretty satisfied with it.

My first nit is in installation. On the top of the microwave are two bolts that are intended to attach through the beams of the cabinet that's over the stove. OK so far. The spacing between these two beams is pretty much standard, since the overhead space is standard to match the width of the stove. OK again. However, the bolts on the microwave are not symmetrical...they don't match the beam location. If your setup is like mine and most houses out there (and my job was a simple replacement of an existing microwave), you will need to attach another support beam under that cabinet to hold the left side of the microwave.

Another item, though this isn't unique to this microwave, is the power cord. It's a standard power cable, so if you want the nice seamless look you'll need to install an outlet somewhere out of sight.

Next nit is the operation. I'm old school - I like to just punch in how many minutes or seconds and hit start. This has a "time saving" interface, in that when you hit "1" it reads as one minute, "2" is two minutes, and so on. But sometimes I want 45 seconds. Sometimes I want 5 minutes and 37 seconds. I'm weird like that. But in order to punch in your own time you have to take an extra step of hitting "cook time" and then key in the time. It's a first world problem, sure, but it's still kind of a pain.

It does a good job of heating things up, the door is wide enough to allow for easy cleaning, and I will say that I've not had any issues with the thing turning on by itself or anything like that. I'm happy with this microwave and I really do think it's a solid product.

product_title: Koldfront Built-In 15 Inch Wide Clear Ice Maker
review_headline: Like others said the sheets don't break up as intended ...
review_body: Ok at first.  A little noisy compared to our old Scotsman.  Came with no instructions what so ever. Just a drain hose and a few clamps in a bag.  Installed unit ok and turned it on.  Ice was made fairly quick and dropped into bin.  Like others said the sheets don't break up as intended so be prepared to stab at the pile of ice to break it into smaller pieces.  Clear restaurant quality ice... not really.  Maybe at first but as the weeks go by the lower quality ice you get.  Hollow cubes with frost like finish.  Certainly not clear.  But who really cares up to this point because ice is ice and it goes in my glass.  The problems started after a month or two when I realized my nice built in under the cabinet installation was in fact leaking even though I had been very careful with the installation and check all connections the first few weeks. Turned out to be a poorly made connection at the factory between the water tray and tube.  I repaired the leak and dried out all the wet wood and floor.  A few months later a loud hum could be heard times.  It was making ice but at a slower pace.  I took it out and checked what I could and finally called repairman.  He changed the start run device and apologized saying the real problem was the cheap compressor and it would probably fail shortly.  Very prophetic young man.  When he returned for another appliance I told him the ice maker quit all together.  He did a quick check and verified the compressor failed.  Wasn't worth the cost to replace.  So there you go it's a 800$ boat anchor slash pile of cheap junk.  I hated to spend another 1800$ on Scotsman but then again the old one lasted for 12 years and did in fact make clear cubes.  Edgestar and Koldfront products appear to be made with the cheapest parts and out together quickly.  I could not recommend this product to anyone.

review_headline: An almost perfect alternative to the traditional washing machine!
review_body:
I have had this washer for a year now and am finally ready to make my judgement.

This is a great lil washer! I got this in a moment of desperation when I moved into my 3rd floor walkup that has no laundry facilities on site. The convenience has really made my life easier! I shudder at the idea of lugging all my and my boyfriends clothes to the nearest laundromat.

It doesn't fit a lot but it's perfect for the basic laundering needs of a couple people. I do a couple loads a week, washing everything from clothes to linens, and hang everything to dry. It can't handle more than two bath towels at a time, but it's totally workable and in fact helps me not slack on consistently washing laundry!

Large items do tend to make it go off balance easier, which can be a bit annoying because you have to adjust the items in there, sometimes multiple times in the same cycle. This mainly happens with full size sheets and duvets. However, it's not hard to do and it's SUCH a small price to pay for the convenience.

Also, I am SO pleased about how clean it gets clothes! I was skeptical it could clean clothes properly (I am extremely picky about this), but honestly I see no difference compared to a normal washer. I love this thing!

Lastly, the price is fair (think how much you'd spend at the laundromat- it paid for itself in about a year for me), it is easy to use and it had a very small footprint. I just leave it in my bathroom next to the sink and use whenever I want!

product_title: LG LDE3037ST Freestanding Electric Double-Oven Range, 30-Inch, Stainless Steel
review_body:
Want to be clear that this review is for the OVEN and the company I bought it from, however ASK WHO will be delivering it. If it's A&M Trucking ("AJ Madison") in the San Francisco/San Jose bay area, READ MY WARNING BELOW.

I am a baker. I'm a stay-at-home-dad and because I like to eat yummy stuff I've had to learn to bake great treats (cooking - not so fun for me; I'm terrible at tracking more than one item at a time; timing). I bought this primarily for the baking functionality - the double oven, the digital panel, and the ability to both set "Cook time" and "Delay start" times. If I could I'd have an oven I could use an app on my phone to activate & control, but that doesn't exist (yet, though I do know for a fact it's being tested). This range is amazing. Just this morning I was standing over it with my coffee in hand wonder what the heck I was ever going to use the warming zone for? I have two kids who are yanking on my clothes anytime I'm preparing food - there's never a need for me to keep food warm, it's one the plates the moment it's done.

Suddenly I had to step outside for a moment and without much thought I turned the warming zone on "Hi" and placed my ceramic mug down on it. When I came back (nearly an hour and 1/2 later... got side tracked) my coffee was nice and hot. Not "burn the roof of your mouth or tongue" hot, but pleasantly hot where you can take a nice sip or small gulp and tolerate the heat. It was awesome.

I had this experience after having the oven for nearly a month already! I was already in love with this oven/range. Like most of my purchases, the wife thought I was insane wanting to spend $1200+ on a range, when we rent an apartment! However it's been very very much worth it. This oven will go anywhere we do - and it's not typical to own your own appliances in the SF bay area when you're a renter.

Worth EVERY PENNY. (FYI - I recommend you get the SquareTrade warranty that comes up as an option upon checkout/cart adding. On-site service for 4 years? Amazing!)

Now, for the shippers. A&M Trucking ("AJ Madison") tried to extort money (cash) out of me upon delivery. I bought from HCcost here on Amazon and THOROUGHLY reviewed all shipping polices and charges PRIOR to purchasing. Knowing we live in an upstairs apartment I scrutinized the HCcost's shipping policies for ANYTHING to do with additional charges for stairs. Nothing. The email they sent me acknowledging my order and delivery status even read, "When your appliance is delivered it will be brought into your room of choice and all packing materials will be collected and removed, if you choose."

When A&M pulled up they informed me there was a charge for stairs. Being no dummy I happily said, "okay, just let me know how much I owe." They pulled the oven off the truck and opened it up so I could inspect - they informed me this was so they didn't carry it all the way up to my place only to have me discover a defect. They then carried the oven up and placed it in my kitchen. After removing a little more packing material from it they took it upon themselves to proclaim they don't normally remove the packing materials but they could for a fee. I explained the policies from where I bought the oven said all packing materials would be removed but said if I needed to return the oven for any reason it might be advisable to keep them just in case. I told them to just leave them downstairs (where they removed 98% of it) and I'd put it in the recycle bin/trash. Then when I walked downstairs with them they said I owed for 47 stairs. They said the first two "flights" were free. I asked what constituted a "flight" and they said 7 stairs is a flight. (Most places recognize 16-18 steps in a flight). I had counted the steps on my way up, 35. Big difference. I told them I had no cash, which they insisted on. I offered to pay bycredit card, but they said, "cash only." This seemed VERY fishy. I told them I never carry cash (I don't, I'm all plastic, all the time). They actually said to me, "Well I wish you would have told us that before we started because we would have never carried the appliance up then." I told them to have their company bill me for anything they believed I owed, as I didn't not contract them for delivery, I simply purchased it from a company who contracted them.

20 minutes later I got a call from someone claiming to be from A&M trucking asking for my credit card number. If the company had any authorization to charge me for anything additional they would already have this information so I told the man I would happily pay anything they felt I owed AFTER I inquired with the company I bought the appliance from. The man got very belligerent all of a sudden. He told me I owed for 47 stairs. I told him they guys who delivered said I got the first two flights free AND that there were only 35 stairs. He told me there 47. I offered to video myself walking up the steps and counting them and to put it on YouTube for him so he could verify. He cursed at me and hung up. After emailing HCcost the details of my problems with A&M Trucking the apologized and confirmed there was not supposed to be any additional shipping or delivery charges.

product_title: SPT Countertop Dishwasher
review_headline: Tired of doing dishes? Check out this life changing machine!
review_body:
The cleaning power of this dishwasher is amazing! The size of the dishwasher is small but the results are great. You can fit a lot more dishes in this washer than you think in the picture. Although because of the small size it has a problem handling large dinner plates that are curved. They fit in the dishwasher and get sparkling clean but you have to hold them in place while you slide the tray into the washer.

I've put crusty oatmeal bowls inside this washer and it got it all off. Coffee stains on the bottom of cups that never came off before are now sparkling white and clean like never before. Silverware comes out cleaner than it was when it was brand new out of the box.

The operation is very quite and it has a cleaner setting for whatever you want to wash and how long you want it to wash. There are eight cleaner cycles. For everyday cleaning I use the speed cleaning cycles because it uses the least amount of water, doesn't use the heater but still cleans the dishes great and the heat from the water dries them. Setup is easy. Plug it in, attach the hot and cold water hoses to the machine, attach the quick-connect to your faucet, attach the machine, turn the cold water on (the water heats the water to the appropriate cleaning temperature), chose your cleaning cycle, push start and there you go.

The one thing I do wish this model had is a button to turn off the heater on every cycle. Only the speed cycle doesn't use the drying cycle. One thing to note is that there are three filters on this dishwasher and all of them are easy to get to, clean out and replace in 5 minutes. If you have a couple of hundred bucks, have a couple of people in an apartment and are tired of doing dishes this thing is a life changer.

review_headline: My wife and I really like it for the most part
review_body:
I bought this 4 months ago. My wife and I really like it for the most part. We have them stacked with the dryer on top. It has good features, but that is where it stops. I now regret purchasing it.

It died on us after only 4 months. I hit the power button and it lit up and then the lights went off and never came back on again. Dead. Turns out the main and secondary control board is broken. This is not even a wear item!

2 chat sessions and 3 phone calls. Honestly, I will never buy a Samsung appliance again. They customer service is awful. They are really bad at training their employees, every time I called I received a different answer.

After the first phone call they said they were going to file a repair claim. Then they called an hour later, which I missed and they sent me an email. The email had a link to check to make sure it was plugged in and it had power. At the bottom of the email it said the claim was being closed. Are you serious! They were going to close the claim without even knowing if it fixed.

Every time I called I gave them the claim number, and they never read any of the notes from the previous discussions. I had to repeat myself every time. I have spent about 2 hours on the phone with them. At the end of the last phone call the had written down the wrong issue, the wrote that it wouldn't turn off.

product_title: GE GTW485ASJWS Energy Star 4.2 Cu.Ft. Top Load Washing Machine with 16 Cycles, White
review_headline: The Worst Washing Machine Every Designed.
review_body:
My machine was purchased from Lowes on December 14, 2012. Lowes finally delivered it on January 4, 2013. The following comments are offered after using it for the past 2.5 months.

1. No matter what load setting is used on initial start, the machine will not put in more than a few inches of water. It requires either filling with a bucket or recycling through another start cycle. If you recycle by pushing the \\"Stop\\" knob, it will beat the clothes with inadequate water resulting in torn clothes. It is best to unplug the machine instead of pushing the \\"Stop\\" knob.

2. If using the hot water setting, the water comes in VERY slowly (water pressure is sufficient and screens are clear) and will not fill to the required setting. Again, either unplug it and fill with a bucket or cycle the timer through the start cycle about 3 times until sufficient water level is assured. The GE repairman came and stated the machine is designed to assure low hot water flow during filling. Someone should inform the designers of their incompetence.

3. Any time the machine is turned off, the agitator will whip the clothes violently. If no one is watching to assure an adequate water level is present, damage to clothes is highly likely. DON'T EVERY LEAVE THIS MACHINE UNATTENDED!

4. When water empties at the end of the wash cycle, it does not spin out the dirty water and soap. This results in retaining a large portion of the soap and dirty water. Therefore, the rinse cycle is immediately contaminated by an unnecessary amount of dirty water.

5. When the rinse cycle begins, the tub will only fill to about 20% of the required rinse water. If left unattended, this results in more clothes damaged due to agitation with very little water. The rinse cycle, again, requires either filling with a bucket or cycling the timer enough times to assure there is sufficient water in the machine.

6. Since the machine failed to spin outthe dirty wash water, it is necessary to start another wash cycle in order to properly rinse the clothes. Without this step, the clothes remain dirty because they were never rinsed in clean water. This extra wash cycle requires the same monitoring and manual addition of extra water to prevent destruction of clothes.

The process of washing a load of clothes takes about 1.5 hours and the machine must be constantly monitored. If the above was the intent of the GE design team, they need to seek other employment.

A positive comment: The machine looks like a normal top-loading washer.

product_title: Bosch 24' Bar Handle Dishwasher 800 Plus Series- Stainless Steel SHX7PT55UC
review_body:
The Bosch 800 Plus Series dishwasher is better than I ever imagined. I can barely hear this thing run, the water draining into the garbage disposal makes more noise than the dishwasher (by the way, plumbing the water outlet on a dishwasher into a garbage disposal is no longer the right way to hook one of these up). This thing has to be twice the size of our old dishwasher. And oh my goodness does it clean dishes, they come out spotless and perfectly clean.

I finally had it with the dishwasher I've hated since the day we moved in, an over 20 year old GE that was a Consumer Reports best buy at the time. I decided it was time for a new dishwasher and refrigerator. I'll cut to the chase - Consumer Reports loves the Bosch Ascenta line, it is their number one best buy recommended dishwashers (there are other brands that tested higher, but were not best buys). The Bosch 800 Plus series finished very well in the rankings, followed by Miele. Consumer Reports says it is not worth the extra money for a stainless steel interior. Given that they loved the GE with a plastic interior, they have held this view for a long time. After looking at each of the models recommended, it became clear that the Bosch 800 Plus was well worth the extra money.

Once I stopped chocking over the price, I narrowed the search down to two dishwashers, the Miele and this Bosch. Compared side by side, there really is no comparison; the Bosch wins in the details. Miele pretty much sets all the rack heights and configuration the way they think you should load the dishwasher. Bosch gives you a ton of flexibility, and after using this machine for a while, I like that flexibility. Bosch also paid more attention to details.

OK, the coolest factor with this dishwasher - frankly one of the reasons I bought it - the cycle time is projected on the floor. I know that sounds really stupid - but it is the coolest thing. The front of this dishwasher has no buttons, no lights, nothing. At the bottom left side there is a yellow LED projector focused on the floor that alternates between a digital clock for the amount of time left in the cycle over a bar graph of progress, and the Bosch logo. There's never a question about how much time is left in the cycle.

This thing holds more dishes than I have ever seen in my life. It used to be a wrestling match to load the old dishwasher, and I could rarely wash colanders or pots. Now I can wash all that stuff along with the regular dishes. I really thought the flappable tines would be stupid, I'd flip them one time and then be done with that. Instead, I find that I use that all the time. It makes it so much easier to load big things or a ton of plates.

There are two top racks in this dishwasher. The top or third rack is for utensils, knives, forks, spoons and other thin things. The grid on the top rack is perfect for lining up utensils so they get perfectly clean. I can get rid of that silly silverware basket that takes up space in the bottom. If you love that basket, Bosch's is brilliant. They made the basket in two parts - it can either be one long basket or the halves can be snapped back to back for a square version. The top rack has two settings, high and low. It's easy to change the height with the two levers on the side of the rack. Setting that rack lower makes room for tea or espresso cups.

The middle rack has three height settings. This is the one for glasses and bowls. Bosch added a flip down shelf on the left side to hold stemware in place, or put cups on the rack. They also include three clips to hold light things in place (it took me a long time to figure out how to snap those clips on).

The bottom rack is super flexible. You can use the silverware basket, or not. There are two rows of tines that can be folded down to put pots on that rack. There is a tall Vee shaped attachment that works for vases or other big things. The middle rack can be removed anda special spray attachment added that will wash really tall things. I can't think of how I would ever use that, but it is an option.

I really like the big hefty handles they put on all the shelves. The racks roll out with an expensive solid feel. The dishwasher detergent and rinse aid dispenser is on the door in the middle. It is very easy to use. The machine will automatically give a message when the rinse aid is low.

You can use any type of dishwasher detergent, power, gel, or tablets. I use the Finish Quantum detergent with great results. With the old machine I stopped using rinse aid with this detergent. The Bosch manual recommends using a rinse aid (the good news, you can adjust how much is used for each wash - more on that in a minute).

The door is kind of amazing. At first I didn't like it very much; I'm used to a door that just falls all the way open once I pull on it. This one takes a little tug to open it and then as you pull it down, the door has some resistance and it stays exactly where you leave it. Because the buttons are all hidden on the top of the door, this is really handy. I can pull the door open a little bit to get at the buttons and don't have to hold the door. The door feels heavy and solid - honestly, it feels expensive and great quality. When the door is pushed all the way up it closes with a satisfying solid click.

It is easy to run this machine. Basically, set it to Auto and be done with it. The only option you might want to use is Sanitize - this will really heat up the rinse water and meets NSF dish sanitation standards. Your dishes will be super-hot when the cycle is finished - so be warned. The Auto wash cycle is long - it starts out at two hours and nine minutes. If the load is light and dishes are relatively clean, it will finish faster. There is a great Rinse mode that takes 9 minutes and uses around a gallon of hot water to rinse the dishes if you are going to delay a wash load. The machine can be set to delay start, you press in the number of hours to delay start. There are a bunch of other cycles like glass, heavy, express, half load, etc. I just use Auto, it works.

Once you've chosen the cycle (the machine remembers the last one chosen) - touch the On / Off button (the buttons are all touch sensitive, they are not true press buttons), press Start for a second until the machine beeps, and then close the door. If everything is good, the timer will light up on the floor. The machine beeps subtly twice when the cycle is done. If you aren't in the room with the machine, you won't hear it.

Now that you've decided to buy one of these, there are some oddities. Installation is really sweet - Bosch gives you most everything you need and uses high quality parts. The electrical junction box is plastic with a sealed electric cord. That cord plugs into the back of the machine. The water connection is a black nylon covered rubber hose that looks like a washing machine hose. The connections are standard compression fittings (if you have a dishwasher already, this hose should work). The drain hose is a little odd; the garbage disposal connection end is the OD as the OD of the garbage disposal hook up. You'll need to lubricate the fitting and wrestle with it a lot to get it connected. The machine has three legs, two in front and one in back. At the front panel there is a flat blade screw slot to raise or lower the rear leg. You'll need to use a wrench on the front two legs. There is a rubber flap that goes behind the front kick plate area. Bosch includes a black metal kick plate panel - you probably won't use that. They did a great thing with the cabinet attachment - you have a choice of attaching the unit with screws on top or the sides. For granite counters this is brilliant.

The dishwasher has a water softener built in. By default it is turned off. The dishwasher comes with a water hardness test strip. I was an analytical chemist for many years; I've never seen a test strip that is worse than this one. Apparently, if a square changes color (or gets dark) that is a positive square. The instructions make it look like the squares will be black and the other will be white. That doesn't happen. I'd strongly encourage you to buy a real set of test strips or have your water tested for hardness (some municipalities will publish hardness - it isn't a required test so you could get lucky).

I determined that my water is slightly hard. I decided to fire up the water softener. You have to purchase salt for dishwashers. This is critical - do not use table salt, rock salt for melting ice, or salt for a home water softener - you will ruin the softener with these things. A bag of salt is $19 at Amazon (Bosch Finish SGZ9091UC Dishwasher Salt). Three quarters of that bag filled the salt reservoir - just enough salt left over that when the salt runs out, I can get by until a fresh bag arrives. I have no idea how long a bag will last - it depends on how hard your water is, how many loads of dishes you wash, and which cycle you use.

In general, the owner's manual is good. Loading options, explanation of the cycles, and tips on how to use it were all very clear.

Now here's the first thing that irritated me about this machine - programming the machine for the water softener and amount of rinse aid to use. Granted, I'm going to do this one time, maybe twice. But darn it the instruction manual is just wrong and confusing for this. Depending on your water hardness, you have to set the softener to the correct number. In order to enter programming mode - hold the Normal button, then press and hold the Start button until the display changes to a letter:00. You will need to cycle through the different modes to set the rinse and softener. Press the Normal button until the correct letter shows up: R is for rinse, H is for the softener (the instructions are actually wrong, they say the setting is with d:00). Now to change the setting for the function, press the Rinse or Express button until the desired number is displayed. Press the Start button or remember the setting.

There's an easy way to think of programming the machine - the Normal button is essentially the Mode button, the Start button is the Enter, and the Rinse and Express are arrow up and down. If Bosch would just put those words in small type on these buttons life would be a lot easier. To enter the programming mode, press and hold down the Normal and Start button.

There are a few other options in that programming menu: r = rinse, h = softener, b = the sound for cycle completion, p = auto power off, s = turn the projector off or on, and d = intensive drying. I've seen some posts on the internet where people are confused by this setting, or can't find it. If your dishes aren't getting dry with the normal settings, enable d, or intensive drying and the final rinse will end up hotter to dry dishes faster.

There is a manual filter in the bottom of the dishwasher. If you see food on that screen, it is really easy to pull out and rinse. An eighth twist of the handle releases it.

I love this dishwasher. At first it is a little complicated to use. I can't believe how quiet this thing is and how many dishes I can load into it. The wash cycle might be long, but it doesn't really matter since I only need to run one load (there are cycle settings to get a faster wash if dishes aren't as soiled). It is also water friendly - the Auto cycle uses between 3.5 and 6.5 gallons of water. That is less than I would use hand washing dishes. A Half Load only uses 2.7 - 4.4 gallons of water. The drain hose is a little odd; the garbage disposal connection end is the OD as the OD of the garbage disposal hook up. You'll need to lubricate the fitting and wrestle with it a lot to get it connected. The machine has three legs, two in front and one in back. At the front panel there is a flat blade screw slot to raise or lower the rear leg. You'll need to use a wrench on the front two legs. There is a rubber flap that goes behind the front kick plate area. Bosch includes a black metal kick plate panel - you probably won't use that. They did a great thing with the cabinet attachment - you have a choice of attaching the unit with screws on top or the sides. For granite counters this is brilliant.

The dishwasher has a water softener built in. By default it is turned off. The dishwasher comes with a water hardness test strip. I was an analytical chemist for many years; I've never seen a test strip that is worse than this one. Apparently, if a square changes color (or gets dark) that is a positive square. The instructions make it look like the squares will be black and the other will be white. That doesn't happen. I'd strongly encourage you to buy a real set of test strips or have your water tested for hardness (some municipalities will publish hardness - it isn't a required test so you could get lucky).

I determined that my water is slightly hard. I decided to fire up the water softener. You have to purchase salt for dishwashers. This is critical - do not use table salt, rock salt for melting ice, or salt for a home water softener - you will ruin the softener with these things. A bag of salt is $19 at Amazon (Bosch Finish SGZ9091UC Dishwasher Salt). Three quarters of that bag filled the salt reservoir - just enough salt left over that when the salt runs out, I can get by until a fresh bag arrives. I have no idea how long a bag will last - it depends on how hard your water is, how many loads of dishes you wash, and which cycle you use.

In general, the owner's manual is good. Loading options, explanation of the cycles, and tips on how to use it were all very clear.

Now here's the first thing that irritated me about this machine - programming the machine for the water softener and amount of rinse aid to use. Granted, I'm going to do this one time, maybe twice. But darn it the instruction manual is just wrong and confusing for this. Depending on your water hardness, you have to set the softener to the correct number. In order to enter programming mode - hold the Normal button, then press and hold the Start button until the display changes to a letter:00. You will need to cycle through the different modes to set the rinse and softener. Press the Normal button until the correct letter shows up: R is for rinse, H is for the softener (the instructions are actually wrong, they say the setting is with d:00). Now to change the setting for the function, press the Rinse or Express button until the desired number is displayed. Press the Start button or remember the setting.

There's an easy way to think of programming the machine - the Normal button is essentially the Mode button, the Start button is the Enter, and the Rinse and Express are arrow up and down. If Bosch would just put those words in small type on these buttons life would be a lot easier. To enter the programming mode, press and hold down the Normal and Start button.

There are a few other options in that programming menu: r = rinse, h = softener, b = the sound for cycle completion, p = auto power off, s = turn the projector off or on, and d = intensive drying. I've seen some posts on the internet where people are confused by this setting, or can't find it. If your dishes aren't getting dry with the normal settings, enable d, or intensive drying and the final rinse will end up hotter to dry dishes faster.

There is a manual filter in the bottom of the dishwasher. If you see food on that screen, it is really easy to pull out and rinse. An eighth twist of the handle releases it.

I love this dishwasher. At first it is a little complicated to use. I can't believe how quiet this thing is and how many dishes I can load into it. The wash cycle might be long, but it doesn't really matter since I only need to run one load (there are cycle settings to get a faster wash if dishes aren't as soiled). It is also water friendly - the Auto cycle uses between 3.5 and 6.5 gallons of water. That is less than I would use hand washing dishes. A Half Load only uses 2.7 - 4.4 gallons of water. And the machine looks great. It also played to my technology side with that projector.

review_headline: Fine if you're not too fussy

For us, the unit is fine. If this model at this price had been unavailable, I probably would not have bought one at all. So, as an entry level wine cellar it is OK.

product_title: Danby DDW497W 23 Countertop Dishwasher - White
review_body:
I find most non-paid reviews either come from those who, for their own reasons, choose to identify themselves as reviewers and, as such review many products - or the frustrated populace who feels screwed by the vendor/product that is in their crosshairs. On occasion, maybe you'll get somebody like me...I don't generally review because most purchased items fall within a median of the superb thing the manufacturer and PR agency says they are, and the devil's joke the poor souls who feel gypped and powerless believe them to be.

I'm only inclined to review this because it fell entirely out of that median. I have abodes on both the east and west coasts. West is my house, new built-in dishwasher always ready to perform. East is a loft in Brooklyn that I've had to furnish on the fly. It came with stove/oven, fridge, sink, counters, cabinets and that's about it. In time an automatic dishwasher seemed like a good idea...nothing permanent, nothing built in. Years ago I bought a vintage hose-to-sink dishwasher from the 1950s at a yard sale. It had a great look but it was worthless in terms of utility.

It was with this in mind when I began to seek out a new hose-to-sink dishwasher for the loft. All the PR trumpeting technological advances in these units got me even more interested, but seriously....I expected an appliance that was marginally better than the '50s model. When I encountered the Danby DDW497W, I liked the approach....green by way of using less electricity, water, and soap than the real built-ins. Its size seemed like a good fit for the loft too, so I bought it.

Nothing in the literature or review prepared me for what I got: the VERY BEST dishwasher of ANY variety I've ever encountered. It's better than any of the many built-ins I've used, including the Whirlpool unit in my West Coast house. I don't believe even Danby expected this....the manual was full of caveats to offset the obvious extrapolations of disappointment. What's so great about this unit? First, all the green stuff is true. It costs a pittance to run. The internal heating element used to up the the hot water temp from the faucet also struck me as a great idea.

When I first hooked it up I was quite nervous about leaks...there were none. The quick-fit faucet adapter worked perfectly as did the basic functionality of the appliance in general. Still, initially I selected the heavy duty wash mode to give the Danby every chance to do the best it could. In that mode, the thing ran for quite a while but when it was finally done, I opened the door, turned the power off, detached it from from the sink, and unplugged it. I'd done the normal dish pre-rinse I always did before running my plates, bowls, implements, etc. through the cycle. I was, nevertheless, surprised to encounter squeaky-clean dishes, silverware, and glassware minus even the hint of a streak. Leap forward to 6 months later: I've stopped cleaning off my dishes at all. I've downgraded the cycle to the lowest (P3) the machine offered - which was considerably faster. I've used the unit once or twice a week since I got it. And no matter what I did, everything I've ever put in this dishwasher came out pristine squeaky clean for a tenth of the cost used to run my dishwasher out west. That would be the end of it but for one thing: because the water pressure was lower than that of the big units, I found I could be very 'creative' with my loading. I was able to nestle things together which in a built-in would surely foretell eventual breakage. Items could touch, lie atop one another...basically break every rule of dishwasher loading and still come out - no hyperbole - SQUEAKY clean. I want the Danby folks to know just HOW satisfied I am because these days underperformance is the norm.

UPDATE: It is now 10/09/12. I've had this dishwasher since 4/12/11. Everything I wrote above still holds...ALL of it. The only thing that seems to have changed is that it appears Danby has discontinued the model. How rare it is in this world that the best example of something is the one that survives, but Danby, why? If the plastic on the door came loose, use another method of attachment. If items fall through, add another strut to the basket. If Ms. Consumer wants a bigger fork basket, just have one made...these are small problems, and me?...well I haven't encountered ANY of them. This Danby dishwasher is still the finest automated dish washing machine I've ever encountered, almost two years after its first use. Hint, if you make those tiny changes, you can change the model number to something new! new! new!

Oh, it just occurred to me...one thing HAS changed. My deluxe, expensive, big-name brand West Coast dishwasher has failed and was replaced while little Danby is still Dandy!

product_title: Frigidaire cooktop
review_body:
Our new cooktop, the Frigidaire FFEC3024LB, fit all of our needs. The best part was the installation process. The instructions were very clear and concise. Not being very familiar in installing a cook top before I began by dismantling the old one in order to disconnect the electrical connections. Don't bother. The new Frigidaire comes with the connections already connected leaving you the only task of connecting the unit to the home's electrical source. Save some time and effort by just disconnecting the old from the wall source and connecting the new in its place. Total time for installation by a do-it-yourselfer was about 45 minutes to and hour. Also, the old cook top fit in the new cook top's packing. Easy for disposal at curbside on garbage pick up day.

In addition I had to trim the opening slightly for the new cook top to fit. It replaced a same size cook top but the dimensions needed were 1/16th of an inch more. A hand sander did the trick and the new stove top fit nicely.

The stove top has performed as expected. The larger controls are nice and are easily removable for cleaning. The controls each have very clear temperature selection stops and a delineated simmer selection that is very handy.

We had considered getting the white model but settled for the black model due to concerns with keeping it looking nice. So far cleaning is a snap and we only use hot water, soft cleaning rag and an occasional small application of dish soap followed by a water only based wipe. Very satisfied.

product_title: BeerTender from Heineken and Krups B95 Home Beer-Tap System
review_headline: Works great , easy to use fun to pour
review_body:
If you love draft beer but don't drink enough to need a full keg this is for you!

I like my beer ice cold poured in a SMALL frozen glass .... I dont drink enough to warrant a full size type draft keg machine with all the hassles that come with it (like Co2) this unit is simple: just drop the draughtkeg in and your done. This unit has a thermostat setting that lets you set it to 36 degrees , the other unit will not allow you to lower the setting so this alone makes it worth the extra $20.

With the draughtkeg and beertender you get a nice little fridge who's sole job is to keep that keg ice cold and easy to pour... since it has a bottom drip tray you can pour your draught \\" english \\" style by letting the first half second just pour out to clear the foam then quickly put your glass in to get a nice pour with little foam - you cant do that when pulling from the big fridge....

What makes it nice is you can pour as much or more importantly as little as you want... like I said I like a small beer glass that gives me nice cold gulps of beer then just pour more - no wasted warm beer just nice and cold PLUS its fun to pour ! Lets face it this is a luxury item because you could just keep it in the big fridge and pour from there but thats no fun! Plus the big fridge is not going to maintain that keg at a constant 36 degrees!

The unit itself is pretty small and very light - it uses some induction type cooling so there is no typical fridge motor its a small fan - now this fan will work hard at first to get that keg down to temp but once its done it gets quieter - its loud enough that you should not put it in an area that is normally quiet .. also since it does not use a fridge type motor it will not work outdoors! It uses the ambient air to help cool the unit - anything over 85 degrees and it will not be able to maintain the temp - so indoor use only.

So to sum up - if you like the Heineken draghtkegs you will enjoy this item - is it necessary ? No , but you will get a much more enjoyable feeling when pouring that perfectly chilled draught. I hope Heineken adds more to the draughtkeg line up like they have in Europe... remember it only works with Heineken so if you dont like Heineken then this item will not work for you...

B95 or B90 ? Spend a little more and get the fancy lcd screen and temp control - especially if you like the cold beer because the other unit is preprogrammed at 39 or 40 deg ... but some people like a warmer draught but the price difference is so little you might as well ' go all the way ' ....

review_headline: Pleased with function and looks but have concerns
review_body:
Installed to vent directly outside thru the wall, 4 inches from back of vent to outside air. Not having to vent thru cabinet above is a huge plus if hung on outside wall.

Pros: Even this smaller (290 cfm) unit throws out a LOT of air! Glad we did not bother with the more powerful 400 cfm version but had to buy the less powerful one to avoid city code requirement for additional makeup air contraption in basement. So far using on the lowest of 4 settings and happy with the quantity of air removed from house. Looks great! Lots of light but remember halogen bulbs throw heat so using the low setting to avoid that.

Cons: Entire vent hoot arrives wrapped in tape to protect stainless surface-- but removing it is like taking off duct tape well burnished on! Unexpectedly hard to remove, and since it was fabricated with the tape applied to all the surfaces before assembly we still can't get into the crevasses to remove the tapelike covering and the ragged remainders show to tall people. Consider not tearing off the tape at seams and using a razor blade to cut it off cleaner. I'm also concerned about winter drafts. This is on a north facing wall and the flap provided with the vent hood doesn't seal off more than 60% of the opening when shut. There is an outside piece (owner provided) that seals completely but it's thin and I'm worried about winter drafts. May have to craft some kind of insert to seal the inside opening (where the air leaves the range hood) better. Also, grills are very flimsy and easy to crease so definitely remove before installing.

product_title: LG WM3455HS 24 Front Load Compact Washer/Dryer Combo , 2.7 cu. ft. Capacity - Silver
review_headline: Wrinkles, wrinkles and more wrinkles.  (Did I mention wrinkles?)
review_body:
Wrinkles badly! I'm a guy, and generally don't care much about a few wrinkles. But we find this machine unacceptable. I really wanted to like this machine, too- thought it would be perfect for our needs.

We bought this combo unit (actually the white one) to put in our dental office to wash our poly/cotton smocks. We've washed them at home for the last 15 years and never had a wrinkling problem, even washing 16-20 at a time. (My home washer is 3.1 cu. ft. capacity, so not much bigger than this machine, but to be fair our dryer has a much bigger capacity.) The washer part of this LG unit works great. But no matter how we set up the dryer, our smocks wrinkled unacceptably. We tried every setting there is. We tried drying 3 smocks at a time. We tried adding a small towel to the smocks. We tried with and without fabric softener. We washed on permanent press and tried lower spin speeds. We tried pulling the smocks out and shaking them before drying. We tried stopping the machine as soon as it said \\"CD\\". We tried letting them go until it beeped after 4 hours. Of course some of the settings and methods caused less wrinkling than others, but all of them were worse than hang drying. And even hang drying them leaves more wrinkles than my unsophisticated male taste would like.

I called LG- they sent a service person out who told me that the unit is working fine and the wrinkling is what you get with condensation drying in a relatively small drum. AC won't take the unit back or exchange it since it is not \\"defective\\". LG won't take it back. We're stuck with a very expensive washing machine. Bottom line is- if you don't mind really wrinkled clothes, or if you don't mind ironing, then this is a good little space saving unit, especially if you don't have a dryer vent. But if you want clothes that aren't so wrinkled that even a guy would notice, then look elsewhere. (BTW- if you want just a washer, LG makes the same unit without the dryerfor $600 less. I would recommend that if you need a washer and have space issues.)
